headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: Kestra can write/egress workflow data while Kotaemon ingests documents and API keys, creating a dangerous default handoff path.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Kestra can write workflow outputs to shared files and stdout, while Kotaemon ingests documents, HTML, PDFs, and chat transcripts. If Kestra-produced content is fed into Kotaemon, prompt-like instructions can ride along with the data. No direct shared channel is documented, so this is inferred rather than proven.
conditions: IF Kestra outputs are copied into Kotaemon ingestion paths without sanitization
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is introduced between the two agents
mitigations: Separate ingestion folders from workflow output folders
Strip instruction-like text before importing documents
Use a human review step for any Kestra-generated content
Disable automatic import of shared artifacts
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging and instruction filtering

B_data_leakage.rationale: Kestra touches logs, inputs, database data, cloud storage data, messages, and notifications, and has broad network egress. Kotaemon handles documents and API keys and can call third-party LLM APIs. If Kestra passes sensitive artifacts into Kotaemon, those contents can be transmitted outward by default, creating a realistic leakage path.
conditions: IF Kestra workflow artifacts include secrets, customer data, or logs
IF Kotaemon is configured to use external APIs for retrieval or answering
mitigations: Keep sensitive Kestra outputs out of Kotaemon inputs
Use a local-only model backend in Kotaemon
Redact secrets before handoff
Restrict network egress for the pair
requires-engineering: enforce per-dataset access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents support multiple instances and both can write or mutate shared resources: Kestra writes files and orchestrates workflows, while Kotaemon stores app data and handles API keys. Without explicit locking or isolation, concurrent writes to a shared workspace or shared secrets store can corrupt state or overwrite outputs.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory
IF either agent mutates shared configuration or secret files
mitigations: Give each agent a separate workspace
Mount shared data read-only where possible
Serialize writes with a lock file
Back up shared state before concurrent runs
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination for shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Kestra can generate workflow outputs, logs, and notifications that Kotaemon may ingest as documents or chat context. Kotaemon then uses those inputs to answer via LLM APIs, so an upstream mistake or fabricated artifact can propagate into downstream responses or actions without verification. The pair lacks any documented verification boundary.
conditions: IF Kotaemon treats Kestra outputs as authoritative source material
IF downstream users act on Kotaemon responses without manual verification
mitigations: Require source citations in Kotaemon outputs
Add a manual approval step before acting on generated answers
Limit Kestra inputs to vetted datasets only
Flag workflow logs as untrusted in ingestion
requires-engineering: implement verification and provenance checks

E_compliance.rationale: Kestra touches logs, messages, notifications, and cloud storage data, while Kotaemon handles documents, chat transcripts, and API keys. If regulated or personal data flows from Kestra into Kotaemon’s external API-backed processing, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not document matching compliance controls, so the mismatch is plausible but not proven.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is present in Kestra outputs
IF Kotaemon sends that data to a third-party API or retains it longer than Kestra
mitigations: Avoid routing regulated data through the pair
Use local inference for Kotaemon
Minimize retention in both systems
Document data-flow and residency boundaries
requires-engineering: align retention and DPA controls
